Simon is the coolest teacher anywhere. Forest Alternative is lucky to have him. books.summary: Pi Patel explains how he was shipwrecked and travels in a lifeboat with a 450 pound Bengal tiger for 227 days, but when they reach Mexico, the tiger escapes into the jungle, and no one believes the story Pi tells them about the tiger. Winner of the 2002 Man Booker Prize for Fiction Pi Patel is an unusual boy. The son of a zookeeper, he has an encyclopedic knowledge of animal behavior, a fervent love of stories, and practices not only his native Hinduism, but also Christianity and Islam. When Pi is sixteen, his family emigrates from India to North America aboard a Japanese cargo ship, along with their zoo animals bound for new homes. The ship sinks. Pi finds himself alone in a lifeboat, his only companions a hyena, an orangutan, a wounded zebra, and Richard Parker, a 450-pound Bengal tiger. Soon the tiger has dispatched all but Pi, whose fear, knowledge, and cunning allow him to coexist with Richard Parker for 227 days lost at sea. When they finally reach the coast of Mexico, Richard Parker flees to the jungle, never to be seen again. The Japanese authorities who interrogate Pi refuse to believe his story and press him to tell them "the truth." After hours of coercion, Pi tells a second story, a story much less fantastical, much more conventional-but is it more true? Life of Pi is at once a realistic, rousing adventure and a meta-tale of survival that explores the redemptive power of storytelling and the transformative nature of fiction. It's a story, as one character puts it, to make you believe in God. Publisher Fact Sheet. A fabulist novel that combines the delight of Kipling's Just So Stories with the metaphysical adventure of Jonah and the Whale.

books.title: Black birds in the sky the story and legacy of the 1921 Tulsa Race Massacre
books.author: Colbert, Brandy
books.summary: "In the early morning of June 1, 1921, a white mob marched across the train tracks in Tulsa, Oklahoma, and into its predominantly Black Greenwood District--a thriving, affluent neighborhood known as America's Black Wall Street. They brought with them firearms, gasoline, and explosives. In a few short hours, they'd razed thirty-five square blocks to the ground, leaving hundreds dead. The Tulsa Race Massacre is one of the most devastating acts of racial violence in US history. But how did it come to pass? What exactly happened? And why are the events unknown to so many of us today? These are the questions that award-winning author Brandy Colbert seeks to answer in this unflinching nonfiction account of the Tulsa Race Massacre. In examining the tension that was brought to a boil by many factors--white resentment of Black economic and political advancement, the resurgence of white supremacist groups, the tone and perspective of the media, and more--a portrait is drawn of an event singular in its devastation, but not in its kind. It is part of a legacy of white violence that can be traced from our country's earliest days through Reconstruction, the Civil Rights movement in the mid-twentieth century, and the fight for justice and accountability Black Americans still face today. The Tulsa Race Massacre has long failed to fit into the story Americans like to tell themselves about the history of their country. This book, ambitious and intimate in turn, explores the ways in which the story of the Tulsa Race Massacre is the story of America--and by showing us who we are, points to a way forward"--From the publisher's web site.

books.title: Days of infamy how a century of bigotry led to Japanese American internment
books.author: Goldstone, Lawrence
books.summary: "On December 7, 1941--'a date which will live in infamy'--the Japanese navy launched an attack on the American military bases at Pearl Harbor, Hawaii. The next day, President Franklin Roosevelt declared war on Japan, and the US Army officially entered the Second World War. Three years later, on December 18, 1944, President Roosevelt signed Executive Order 9066, which enabled the Secretary of War to enforce a mass deportation of more than 100,000 Americans to what government officials themselves called 'concentration camps.' None of these citizens had been accused of a real crime. All of them were torn from their homes, jobs, schools, and communities, and deposited in tawdry, makeshift housing behind barbed wire, solely for the crime of being of Japanese descent. President Roosevelt declared this community 'alien,'--whether they were citizens or not, native-born or not--accusing them of being potential spies and saboteurs for Japan who deserved to have their Constitutional rights stripped away. In doing so, the president set in motion another date which would live in infamy, the day when the US joined the ranks of those Fascist nations that had forcibly deported innocents solely on the basis of the circumstance of their birth. In 1944 the US Supreme Court ruled, in Korematsu v. United States, that the forcible deportation and detention of Japanese Americans on the basis of race was a 'military necessity.' Today it is widely considered one of the worst Supreme Court decisions of all time. But Korematsu was not an isolated event. In fact, the Court's racist ruling was the result of a deep-seated anti-Japanese, anti-Asian sentiment running all the way back to the California Gold Rush of the mid-1800s. Starting from this pivotal moment, Constitutional law scholar Lawrence Goldstone will take young readers through the key events of the 19th and 20th centuries leading up to the fundamental injustice of Japanese American internment. Tracing the history of Japanese immigration to America and the growing fear whites had of losing power, Goldstone will raise deeply resonant questions of what makes an American an American, and what it means for the Supreme Court to stand as the 'people's' branch of government"--Provided by the publisher.

books.summary: "For ten years, Achut Deng surrived at Kakuma Refugee Camp in Kenya after her family was ripped apart by the Second Sudanese Civil War. But Achut wanted to do more than merely survive. She wanted to live. The twenty-two-year civil war essentially orphaned over 20,000 children and drove them from their villages in southern Sudan. Some of these children walked over a thousand miles, through dangerous war zones and across unforgiving deserts. They are often referred to as The Lost Boys. But there were girls, too. Achut Deng was one of them. This is her story. It's a story of unimaginable hardship and selfless bravery, of tormenting physical pain and amazing emotional resilience, of unbreakable bonds of friendship and family. It's a story about what happens when your dream comes true, only to give way to a new nightmare. It's about how hard you will fight to save your own life"--Provided by publisher.

books.title: I am the cage
books.author: Grant, Allison Sweet
books.summary: Nineteen-year-old Elisabeth Amos decides to forego college to escape her mother and painful memories from a series of childhood surgeries. Escaping to a tiny cabin in a small Wisconsin town, Elisabeth mostly keeps to herself, until a snowstorm and power outage force her to befriend a local sheriff who is her neighbor. Through their relationship, she learns to see the beauty inside herself and gains the bravery to confront her past.

books.title: Just until
books.author: Moldover, Joseph
books.summary: Seventeen-year-old Hannah Lynn is ready to get out of Evans Beach, Maine, and all the bad memories it holds. But when her estranged older sister Pauline's two sons are taken by the state, Hannah and her father Larry become the only thing keeping them out of the foster care system. Larry promises that they will only have to take care of the boys for a little while, until Pauline can get back on her feet, but Hannah knows it won't be easy for Pauline to do so. Hannah soon finds herself developing a deeper connection with her nephews, and when the unthinkable happens, Hannah is soon forced to make a difficult decision.

Her life is further complicated when the jilted prince and an assassin sent to kill Lia arrive at the village as well, each in disguises of their own, and romance blossoms unexpectedly between Lia and the two young men.

Slowly, Evie soon starts to make progress with the help of caregivers and peers who are fighting their own disordered-eating battles, and she finds a way to love herself again.

As rehearsals and press obligations intensify, Marisol must negotiate on- and off-camera rivalries, an eccentric director's demands, and the risks of falling for a nontraditional actress in the limelight.

books.title: The poetry of car mechanics
books.author: Stemple, Heidi E. Y.
books.summary: After his mother left as a result of her mental illness, fifteen-year-old Dylan was forced to move in with his grandfather, who doesn't understand him. The only place he feels at home is in his grandfather's auto shop and in the woods behind it, where he enjoys bird watching and writing poetry. But when he rescues an injured red-tailed hawk one day, it transforms his life and leads him to finally make a friend and discover an inner strength he didn't know he had.
books.subjects_text: Family problems Mental illness Birds Automobile mechanics Domestic fiction. Novels in verse.

books.title: The rebel's guide to Pride
books.author: Hubbard, Matthew
books.summary: Zeke Chapman has spent his young life living in his image-obsessed father's shadow, hiding who he really is, but when he comes out as gay, he becomes determined to follow his own path. So when his best friend, Sawyer, begs him to help the QSA plan Pride Day, he agrees because he knows it will upset his father, but things get complicated when the mayor announces an ordinance that cancels all LGBTQ+ celebrations. Soon, Zeke begins planning a series of underground "Pride Speakeasies" and finds his voice to stand up for what he believes in.
books.subjects_text: Prejudices Sexual minorities Gay pride celebrations LGBTQ people Pride celebrations Alabama

books.title: The romance rivalry
books.author: Lee, Susan
books.summary: Loving romance novels as much as she does, making a career as an online book reviewer is a dream come true for Irene Park. Unfortunately, her real-life dating story has yet to appear, and seems like it may never be written at all. Then Aiden Jeon, her online review rival and nemesis, issues a challenge--they will both try to find love by romance novel trope, and whoever finds it first wins.

books.title: Royal blood
books.author: Carter, Aimée
books.summary: Seventeen-year-old American girl Evan Bright has grown up with a royal secret--she is the illegitimate daughter of the King of England. Now, forced to spend a summer with her father and the royal family, who don't like the fact she even exists, Evan finds her secret outed to the world. A fun night turns deadly, and Evan suddenly becomes caught up in a murder investigation.
books.subjects_text: Americans Inheritance and succession Kings and rulers Homicide Rumor Secrecy Mystery fiction.

books.title: Sanskari sweetheart
books.author: Devarajan, Ananya
books.summary: Indian American high school senior Raina Iyer needs to win the National Bollywood Dance Circuit Scholarship to show her mother that dance can be a financially stable career. However, her long-time boyfriend and co-captain, Aditya, breaks up with her right before their performance and their dance routine tanks on stage, with Raina suffering a head injury. When Raina wakes up the next day, she finds she's in a time loop and she has the chance to redo the day. But each time Raina tries to do everything perfectly, she is dumped and humiliated over and over again. Raina wonders if perfection isn't the key to breaking out of the time loop.

books.title: Sisters of sword & song
books.author: Ross, Rebecca
books.summary: Sisters Evadne and Halcyon haven't seen each other in eight years, since Halcyon has been serving in the queen's army. The day before she's scheduled to return, Halcyon shows up in Eva's bedroom, falsely accused of murdering another soldier. Halcyon is sentenced to a grueling labor camp, and Eva, who begged to help fulfill half of Halcyon's sentence, becomes a servant girl to the murdered soldier's family. There, Eva learns that her sister and the murdered soldier were undertaking a dangerous mission to recover a powerful relic from the gods, and sets out to clear her sister's name.
books.subjects_text: Sisters Relics Gods and goddesses Magic Fantasy fiction.

books.title: A study in drowning
books.author: Reid, Ava
books.summary: Effy Sayre is the only female architecture student at the university of Llyr. While she excels, her dream is to study literature and her favorite author, Emrys Myrddin, who wrote the epic novel "Angharad," but women are denied entry into that program. Fate seems to give her a break when she hears of and wins a contest to redesign the Myrddin family estate. Arriving to discover the estate crumbling to the ground and a near-impossible task to salvage it, Effy also discovers literature student Preston Héloury, who is determined to prove that Emrys didn't write the epic novel. When he asks for Effy's help in his endeavor, she agrees, hoping it will gain her entry into the literature program. Together the pair begin their investigation, but soon discover things aren't right at the estate, and that the tale, featuring a cruel fairy king and the mortal woman that broke his heart, may be more truth than fiction.
books.subjects_text: Contests Haunted houses Fairies Good and evil Magic College students Fantasy fiction. Romance fiction. Mystery fiction.

books.subjects_text: Cooking, French Cooking French cooking Cooking Cookbooks.

books.title: Summer girls
books.author: Dugan, Jennifer
books.summary: Cass lives in the beach town of Newport, and she isn't looking forward to the beginning of the summer as it means the arrival of summer girls, the obnoxious daughters of the rich who stay in their families' summer homes, sail their yachts, and make life insufferable for the working-class families that live there year round. Birdie is the daughter of a wealthy real estate developer dad and a social media influencer mom, and as punishment for crashing her boyfriend's expensive car after a very messy breakup, she's forced to work as a beach parking lot attendant for the summer. Cass, whose dad works for Birdie's father, is enlisted to keep an eye on Birdie and keep her out of trouble, but despite her initial animosity towards Birdie, she realizes that the other girl isn't so bad. As they spend more and more time together, their friendship turns to something more, causing Cass to question her rule of never dating summer girls.
books.subjects_text: Lesbians Wealth City and town life Romance fiction.

books.title: This is not a dead girl story
books.author: Sweeney, Kate
books.summary: Sixteen-year-old awkward Jules is best friends with her beautiful cousin Remy, seventeen, and Remy's handsome boyfriend River, whom Jules has had a crush on for years. When River suddenly dies in a car accident and Remy disappears a week later, Jules decides to search for her, even though most people think Remy has died. Joining with River's cousin Sam, Jules digs into Remy's disappearance, River's death, and the secrets the town has been keeping.
books.subjects_text: Missing persons Secrets Cousins Mystery fiction.

books.title: Top heavy
books.author: Dechambeau, Rhonda
books.summary: After spending a grueling summer perfecting their dance skills, best friends Esme, fifteen, and Mia start the school year with a bang by earning envy-inducing spots on Miss Regina's Elite dance team. That bang turns into a nightmare when Esme realizes they took the spots of two popular dancers, and the rest of the team resents them for it; when her dad, out of work for months, begins to struggle to put food on the table; when a stranger during a night out touches her breasts without warning or permission. Feeling oversexualized for her large chest all her life, this event finally makes Esme snap, throwing her off her dance abilities and feeling separated from her loved ones. She needs to find something to hold on to to pull her back up so she can soar on the dance stage again. A novel in verse.
books.subjects_text: Self-actualization (Psychology) Sexual assault Dance Friendship Self-realization Sex crimes Novels in verse.

books.title: True life in Uncanny Valley
books.author: Caletti, Deb
books.summary: Eleanor's father Hugo Harrison is the brilliant and charismatic tech genius whose AI inventions seem to create a new, better reality, but since her birth was the result of an affair her mother had with Hugo years ago, she's always had to watch her father from afar. So when she sees a posting for a live-in summer nanny job for Hugo's young son--her half-brother--she knows she has to apply. As she begins working for her father, Eleanor begins to see just how much of her father's picture-perfect life is a lie, and the new invention he's working on could change how humans interact with technology forever.
books.subjects_text: Fathers and daughters Father-daughter relationship Truthfulness and falsehood Deception Family life Family secrets Man-woman relationship Technological innovations

books.title: What we wish for
books.author: Maysonet, Melody
books.summary: For fifteen-year-old Layla Freeman, life has become one big game of pretending her mother and she are not living out of a homeless shelter, keeping that a secret from her classmates, believing it is only temporary. When her mom, who was thirty days sober, overdoses yet again, Layla goes to her rich aunt and uncle as a last resort, who, in spite of their feud, take Layla in and pay for her mother's fancy rehab stay. Everything seems looking up for Layla, until living in her aunt and uncle's mansion starts straining her relationship with her best friend--and then she uncovers one secret that could destroy her new and old worlds all at once.
books.subjects_text: Families Secrecy Teenage girls Drug abuse Family life Homelessness Bildungsromans.

books.title: While we're young
books.author: Walther, K. L.
books.summary: Once an inseparable trio, Grace, Isa, and Everett separated after what they call the infamous "Freshman Year Fracture," when Everett broke Isa's heart, leaving Grace, who has secretly loved Everett forever, with nowhere to go. Meanwhile, Isa has been secretly hanging out with James, Grace's brother, which could fracture their friendship forever. The cure, Grace thinks, is to convince Isa to help her kidnap Everett and escape James for a while for a senior skip day in Philadelphia, where every romantic thread will come together.
